stories.title: New RL method gives turn-level credit to streaming video agents
stories.summary: Researchers propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video models that assigns credit per turn instead of per trajectory, addressing a flaw where shared credit reinforces redundant replies after success and discourages useful follow-ups after failure.
stories.more: Streaming video models must repeatedly decide whether to respond or keep observing, and existing GRPO-based approaches apply a single trajectory-level advantage across all turns. The paper argues this shared credit scheme is flawed: it can reinforce redundant replies after an earlier success and discourage useful follow-up responses after an earlier failure. TurnWise instead computes credit at the level of individual turns rather than whole trajectories. The excerpt does not give benchmark results or the model sizes tested.

stories.title: NEO-VLA lets robot action policies read evolving visual computation directly
stories.summary: NEO-VLA is a vision-language-action model that lets action policies access evolving visual computation directly, rather than relying on a frozen set of features from a separate visual encoder, aiming to preserve signals like geometry and subtle state changes manipulation needs.
stories.more: Most vision-language-action models compress perception with a visual encoder before action reasoning begins, a fixed endpoint that can discard signals manipulation depends on, such as local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. NEO-VLA instead gives the action policy direct access to the visual encoder's evolving computation rather than a single compressed snapshot. The paper frames this as a question of whether action policies should inherit a fixed visual endpoint or access live visual processing. The excerpt does not specify the model's size, training data, or benchmark results.

stories.title: GameVerse dataset targets minute-scale gameplay for world models
stories.summary: GameVerse is a new gameplay video dataset built to extend interactive world models beyond roughly a minute of coherent rollout, using longer clips and more detailed captions than prior datasets of under-ten-second clips with coarse, whole-clip text.
stories.more: Interactive world models can generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs, but current models lose coherence after about a minute of rollout. The paper attributes this to a lack of long-horizon training data rather than model capacity, noting that existing gameplay datasets use clips under ten seconds with coarse captions describing the whole clip. GameVerse addresses this with minute-scale gameplay clips and more granular captions intended to support longer-horizon modeling. The excerpt does not give the dataset's size or which games it covers.

stories.title: FrontierPhysics benchmark tests AI agents on real physics research tasks
stories.summary: FrontierPhysics is a new benchmark of 56 tasks, built by 42 physicists from their own research, that evaluates AI agents on end-to-end physics research rather than fixed questions or isolated sub-tasks, and checks research quality alongside correctness.
stories.more: Existing physics benchmarks for AI agents typically test fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely assess research quality itself. FrontierPhysics introduces 56 tasks created by 42 physicists based on their own research, spanning nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires an agent to carry out research-like work rather than answer a predetermined question. The excerpt does not report how current agents score on the benchmark.

stories.title: Study: multi-turn RL mainly improves LLM agents' error recovery
stories.summary: A new study finds that multi-turn reinforcement learning's gains for LLM agents depend heavily on how much interaction budget is allowed, and that it mostly improves error recovery and long-horizon behavior rather than uniformly raising single-step decision quality.
stories.more: The researchers evaluate multi-turn agentic RL using Pass@(K,T) across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T, finding that trajectory-level RL advantages require sufficiently large turn budgets and shrink sharply as those budgets tighten. They also find RL's benefit is not a uniform lift in single-step decision quality; instead, it concentrates in a model's ability to recover from errors over long interactions. The excerpt is cut off before describing the specific tasks or models tested.

stories.title: LLM agent acts as teleoperator to generate robot training data cheaply
stories.summary: PyRUA-DataFarm has a coding agent take over the robot teleoperator's job: given a data request and one calibration episode, it rebuilds the task in simulation by writing the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge, cutting the cost of collecting robot demonstrations.
stories.more: Teleoperation is the standard way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs operator and robot time, and every new task starts from scratch. DataFarm asks whether a coding agent can replace the teleoperator: given a data request and a single calibration episode of the robot in the target scene, the agent rebuilds the task in simulation by writing the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. The simulator then supplies exact actions for the task. The excerpt cuts off before describing how the generated data compares to real teleoperated data.

stories.title: StreamDuo pairs a live commentator AI with a game-wiki research agent
stories.summary: StreamDuo addresses cross-game streaming commentary, where models trained on one game struggle to transfer game-world knowledge to games they've never seen, by pairing a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played.
stories.more: Streaming video LLMs can already commentate live gameplay, but they are typically trained and tested on the same games. The researchers study cross-game commentary and find that current commentators transfer their sense of timing but not their knowledge of the game world to unseen games. StreamDuo combines a trainable commentator model with a frozen research agent that consults the wiki of whatever game is being played, feeding it game-specific knowledge the commentator lacks. The excerpt is cut off before describing how the two components combine their outputs or how StreamDuo performs against single-model baselines.

stories.title: Big Tech's AI data center spending keeps rising despite unclear returns
stories.summary: After Q3 earnings calls from four major AI competitors, The Verge reports Big Tech's data center buildout for AI keeps growing with no sign of slowing, even though the spending has not yet produced the returns it was supposed to deliver.
stories.more: Four of the biggest competitors in the AI race held quarterly earnings calls in late October, and two things are clear from them: Big Tech is not done spending record amounts on AI data centers, and that buildout is no closer to producing the returns it was supposed to yield.
